findings.title: Translate only loads current locale, can cache missing translation
findings.body: I18n.translate in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb only calls load_locale(config.locale) before delegating to the backend, but the new fallback chain is [user locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en]. If the fallback locale files are not yet loaded the backend lookup misses and returns 'translation missing'. That result is stored in the global LRU cache. Any code path that did not run ApplicationController#set_locale (Sidekiq jobs, mailers, console, standalone backend calls) can therefore poison the cache, and later web requests that did preload fallbacks will still hit the cached missing string until LRU eviction or reload!.

findings.title: Fallback lookup hits SiteSetting on every translation without normalization
findings.body: FallbackLocaleList#[] in config/initializers/i18n.rb is called by the I18n fallbacks backend on every translated key and executes [locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact. That means every I18n.t does a SiteSetting read plus allocation. With hundreds of translations per page this is significant overhead. It also never normalizes the incoming locale to a symbol, so a string 'en' and symbol :en are not deduped by uniq, producing duplicate chain entries, and string entries never match the symbol entries in @loaded_locales, causing repeated load_path scans.

findings.title: Translation cache key ignores fallback chain
findings.body: The LRU key in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb is built only from key plus config.locale plus backend object_id. The rendered value now depends also on SiteSetting.default_locale, which is part of the fallback chain. Changing the site default locale or updating a fallback-locale translation does not invalidate existing entries, so users whose own locale misses will keep seeing the old fallback string until the entry is evicted, reload! is called, or the process restarts.
